notes:
VX Prime+ is Telos Alliance's entry-tier (8-hybrid) VoIP "talkshow" telephone-hybrid engine for broadcast studios; it shares an identical 1U rear-panel hardware platform with the VX Enterprise (differing only in licensed hybrid/fader capacity: 8 vs up to 120). Specs and rear-panel port list (page 18) and Specifications appendix (pages 71-73) were taken from Telos Alliance's own official "VX Enterprise and VX Prime+ User's Manual," v1.4, July 2024 (hosted on a Telos Alliance-owned S3 bucket, fetched over verified HTTPS). Official product landing page: https://www.telosalliance.com/Telos/VX-Prime-Plus (marked "legacy" but still the current listing; lacks a full port-level spec table, hence the manual PDF was used as the primary source).

Important: the VX Engine itself carries NO direct analog or AES3 audio I/O — all studio audio is Livewire+/AES67 over the LAN Ethernet port. Physical analog/AES3 audio breakout is done via separate Telos Alliance "xNode" appliances (not part of this device), so no analog/AES audio ports are listed here. Dimensions confirmed as 1.75"H x 19"W x 15.5"D (1RU). RS-232, IPMI, USB, and VGA ports are all explicitly documented by Telos as development/diagnostic/factory-only, not for end-user use, but are physically present per the manual's rear-panel diagram — their connector types beyond RS-232's obvious DB9-style serial and VGA's DB15 are reasonably standard assumptions; IPMI and USB connector types are inferred (flagged individually) since the manual's rear-panel photo is too low-resolution to positively confirm each labeled point (A-G) against its numbered description.

ports.name: AC Power In 2
ports.note: Dual hot-swappable, redundant, internal auto-ranging supplies, 90-132/187-264 VAC 50/60Hz, IEC receptacle with internal fuse; system power consumption 150W (rear-panel silkscreen references 400W OEM supply modules, but rated system draw per Specifications is 150W)

ports.name: LAN
ports.note: 100/1000BASE-T; carries Livewire+/AES67 AoIP studio audio, PoE-fed VSet controllers, and system control traffic

ports.name: WAN
ports.note: 100/1000BASE-T; connects to SIP/ISP telephony network or local PBX, isolated from LAN multicast, disabled by default

ports.name: RS-232
ports.note: Manual states 'for development and diagnostic purposes only'

ports.name: IPMI Control Port
ports.note: Manual states 'a connection for development purposes only'; connector type inferred as RJ-45 (standard dedicated IPMI management LAN on this 1U server platform) since the manual does not explicitly state the connector

ports.name: USB Ports
ports.note: Rear-panel legend labels these 'USB Ports' but the accompanying text unusually calls them 'serial ports used for development and factory production only'; exact port count and USB revision are not stated, so connector type/count are a best-effort inference from the low-resolution rear-panel diagram

ports.name: VGA
ports.note: Manual states 'used for development and diagnostic purposes only'
